In #40901 I re-state various existing theorems in topology in terms of ZeroDimensionalSpace, which is itself defined in terms of an WithBot ℕ∞-valued smallInductiveDimension.

Small problem - the most basic file which defines the order instance on ℕ∞ also defines instances for MonoidWithZero, IsOrderedRing, etc., which triggers a bunch of assert_not_exists scattered throughout topology files. What's to be done here? I don't think it's unreasonable that a file that knows about say, Baire spaces, also knows about the extended naturals.
(On a similar note, why is ENat not defined as an abbrev? That would sidestep this whole problem.)
It's similar to the challenges of refactoring things to use PNat. I would suggest a yak shave, and separate the ENat definitions and the deriving MonoidWithZero etc to separate files.

Congrats @Violeta Hernández on your effort to officially introduce zero dimensional spaces to mathlib!
In my work
https://github.com/yannpequignot/lean-wqo-continuous-functions
I ended up formalizing some properties of 0-dim spaces which were absent of mathlib, if I am not mistaken. For example, any countable metrizable space can be embedded into the rationals (Sierpinski) and therefore is 0-dim. I am just curious if this is part of your PR or if it could be an interesting addition. As of now, I worked with the existence of a basis of clopen, but I am interested in understanding the implications of defining them with the small inductive dimension.
My PRs are quite basic in scope. You're welcome to PR this result once docs#ZeroDimensionalSpace lands!
We do have the fact that rationals are zero-dimensional, at least indirectly, via docs#CompletelyRegularSpace.isTopologicalBasis_clopens_of_cardinalMk_lt_continuum

Even after the Data.ENat.Basic split, I'm still running into problems. The file for Metrizable spaces has an assert_not_exists for AddMonoidWithOne, so that it doesn't import real numbers. This means that I can't even import Data.ENat.Basic, which imports Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Sub.WithTop in order to define ENat subtraction.

I think it'd be quite more reasonable to replace this with an assert_not_exists for the reals themselves.

The reason I make this AddMonoidWithOne instead of Real in #27946 is because it's not the real numbers themselves that are a large import, but all the ordered algebra that it transitively implies. And I've also seen assert_not_exists AddMonoidWithOne in many other files to ensure they don't import any ring theory. Perhaps instead we can make this something like DivisionSemiring or IsOrderedRing (or both) instead?
